comparator.name: Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Current permitted revisit on 2026-11-13. The current after-revision 2026–2027 PER and Course Guide PDFs are byte-identical to the prior reviewed versions; the curriculum page visible text is unchanged. This is the English-taught, full-time AUBS programme. AUDE remains the neutral first formal track, selected independently of UCR fit. The first-year architectural project is one valid choice coherent with AUDE; other tracks and indicative Binder/Climber/Digger strategies are not combined. PER Article 3.4 and its table (pp21–23) specify 125 core EC, including 7P1B30 at 5 EC and 7A2B30 at 10 EC. Adding 10 ITEC and Appendix 2 electives of 40 EC (15 in Year 2, 25 in Year 3) yields 175 EC, with years 60/60/55. Article 3.4(8) instead requires at least 45 elective EC. The Course Guide (pp12–13) specifies both Year 3 projects at 10 EC and 130 core + 10 ITEC + 40 elective = 180 EC. Two separately graded project parts and a two-quarter span do not establish an adopted 5+5 core/elective split. Appendix 3 changes level requirements, without reconciling project weight or elective volume. The current regulations index still links the same after-revision PER, separately from the inapplicable before-revision edition; no linked credit amendment or explicit precedence was found. Current Examination Committee Regulations Article 1.3 provides programme/elective approval powers within the PER framework, without a specific project-credit correction or elective-volume reconciliation. Individual approval or exemption is not assumed. The official public Osiris URL returned an app shell, without a readable credit payload; this access limit is separate from the academic contradiction. Independent rules remain supported: 4CBLW00 after relevant embedded P&PD; 7P1B30 after at least three of four Year 2 projects; BEP after 120 EC including compulsory Year 1, all Year 2 project-line projects and all multidisciplinary projects. No exceptional permission is assumed. The pilot requires 45 EC at level 3 overall and 30 elective EC at levels 2/3, including 5 EC at level 3. Nonoverlap, approval of a 180 EC PlanApp after 90 EC earned, BSA 45/60, embedded P&PD and noncredit SG/MyFuture requirements remain verified. Preserve the supported 25-component, 130 EC public subset and the verified interest/course research. Complete degree and UCR comparability remain unapproved; see detailed revisit evidence.

exception.reason: Reconcile current AUDE 7P1B30 Multidisciplinary Project credits and elective volume. Current Course Guide pp12–13 explicitly says both third-year projects are10EC, giving130core+10ITEC+40elective=180. Current formal PER Article3.4/table pp21–23 instead specifies125core and7P1B30=5EC, while Article3.4(8) says at least45electives and Appendix2 says40(15Y2+25Y3). Appendix3 pilot changes level requirements, not project credits or total elective volume. Need authoritative amendment, explicit precedence or reconciliation; do not invent5EC.
exception.curriculumContext: English-taught full-time current after-revision AUDE route, selected by official track order independently of UCR fit. Current named formal core125 including5ECMultidisciplinaryProject,10ITEC andAppendix2open40 yields175(60/60/55), not a certified180ECpathway. CourseGuideexplicit10ECproject would close180but materially conflicts with formal5EC/table125 andgeneral45elective rule. Both current sources and pilot checked; no missing credit or exception assumed.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Fresh actual24-course180EC ecological/spatial-planning and built-environment sustainability attempt reviewed internally against current workbook. Full weight given to nature-based infrastructure design, actual materials/mechanics/thermodynamics laboratories, GIS/spatial engineering, circularity, energy modelling/design, stakeholder research and consumer prototyping. This is a substantive urban/environment segment, not proof of full architectural studio, building physics, structural engineering or real-estate training. Programme-level comparability remains provisional pending external reconciliation; no no-match disposition.

audience.programmeDescription: This English-taught TU/e degree studies buildings and cities through design, engineering, environmental performance and the needs of their users. The Architectural Urban Design and Engineering pathway develops architectural and urban design through projects, history, technology and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The published project credits and elective requirements conflict, so a complete degree pathway and UCR comparison cannot yet be confirmed. This does not establish that UCR has no relevant programme.

curriculum.limitation: The supported components shown total 130 EC: 60 in year 1, 45 in year 2 and 25 in year 3. The multidisciplinary project and elective space are omitted because their published credit requirements conflict. This is an incomplete degree pathway; a complete UCR comparison awaits clarification.

componentNotes.7P4AB10: One first-year project choice is shown. The later AUDE route requires its own subject and project courses; other tracks are not combined into this pathway.
componentNotes.7A2B30: Entry normally requires at least 120 EC, all compulsory first-year components, all second-year project-line projects and all multidisciplinary projects. The multidisciplinary project must be completed first.
componentNotes.0LVX10: The first-year study-advice threshold is normally 45 of 60 EC. Personal and professional development is embedded in credited courses; five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities with a total value of seven are additional non-credit requirements.
